messages:
claire: quick experiment today: borrowed a friend's Starlink and mounted it on my 3rd-floor balcony for a midday test. figured i'd try if it beats my usual cable ISP during peak hours. photos + raw speedtest below 📸

diego: oooh photos pls :camera_with_flash:

claire: uploading... (2 pics)
  - one of the dish on the railing, one of the view (tiny pigeons)

claire: speedtest results (one run):
```
PING: 28 ms
DOWNLOAD: 182.4 Mbps
UPLOAD: 15.7 Mbps
JITTER: 4 ms
```

yasmin: that's actually really decent for midday. how's latency to our dev host?

claire: ran a quick traceroute to app.redwood.dev: first hop ~10ms, then 32ms -> final 35ms. felt snappy in a quick video call too.

marta: balcony life > basement den. also, did you tether on battery or plug the router in? curious re: stability.

claire: starlink plugged into AC (apartment balcony outlet through a GFCI). battery was a no-go for a long call.

diego: wild. any weird packet loss or dropouts while you were running it?

netbot: [automated] Between 2317654335 and 2317654350 observed 0.2% packet loss to external test host 8.8.8.8 when routed via Starlink gateway. No service disruptions reported.

yasmin: 0.2% is fine for casual meetings but might trip up prod demos. also, birds sound in background? :bird:

claire: lol the pigeons were photobombing. audio handled with USB mic + noise gate so it wasn't bad.

marta: were there any interference issues with the neighbor's wifi? rural? urban?

claire: pretty urban; surrounding APs but Starlink handles link aggregation on its side.

diego: this makes me want to try satellite as a backup for my nightly deploy window. anyone done automatic failover from cable -> starlink?

marta: we used a cheap dual-WAN router last year, did 30s failover. works but depends on DNS-caching behavior of clients.

claire: poll: what should i do for permanent setup? (1) keep Starlink as primary on balcony, (2) keep cable as primary + Starlink as backup, (3) return the dish and stick with cable. vote with emoji 1️⃣ 2️⃣ 3️⃣

diego: 2️⃣ - redundancy is nice

yasmin: 1️⃣ - vibes and speed 🌊

marta: 2️⃣ - but put router on UPS if you rely on it during power flickers

claire: noted. i'll test a week as backup and maybe try automatic failover on a small router.

otterbot: [reminder] Starlink dishes should have >= 30cm clearance from obstructions. Checkout community guide: http://tiny.cc/starlink-hints

netbot: [info] Local ISP "CableStream" reports planned maintenance later today 2317654900-2317658500 UTC. Expect brief reconnects for on-prem modems.

diego: ugh that maintenance window will be when my overnight CI runs. maybe i'll enable the backup link too.

yasmin: someone should make a leaderboard: "most dramatic WFH connectivity fix". claire gets points for balcony mount + pigeons.

marta: awarded: 5 aesthetic points, 3 reliability points.

claire: i'll leave the dish for the week and post follow-up stats. also, will not invite pigeons to standups unless requested 😂
